channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: Improvements on the pull request overview in public preview
item.description: Your feedback has helped improve the new pull request Overview page since its November 5, 2026 public preview. Here’s what’s new!

item.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
item.description: Learn how OpenAI built the Performance Factory, a system of Codex-powered workflows that finds and fixes performance issues to help keep ChatGPT fast.

item.title: GPT-Live-1.1, describe in plain language when to delegate
item.description: GPT-Live-1.1 improves pronunciation, accent consistency, and transcription in multilingual voice conversations. Use gpt-live-1.1 in an existing Live session configuration and describe in plain language when to delegate to your backend.

item.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
item.description: Give your agents access to hundreds of tools while using fewer tokens with Tool Retrieval, now in preview in the Gemini API.

item.title: Wait for pull request events with GitHub CLI
item.description: GitHub CLI now supports GitHub Event Streams. With gh v2.105.0, you and your agents can wait for a pull request to change with a single command instead of polling it in a loop.

item.title: How Sumitomo Life’s leaders helped teams adopt ChatGPT Enterprise
item.description: Sumitomo Life uses ChatGPT Enterprise to research insurers, prepare proposals, and draft code for investment analysis. Early use by executives helped drive adoption.

item.title: Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
item.description: OpenAI measures how coding agents are accelerating AI research, where their performance remains uneven, and what this signals about recursive self-improvement.

item.title: Managing frontier AI risk: From training to deployment
item.description: OpenAI explains how it manages frontier AI risk from training through deployment with model alignment, sandboxing, blocking safeguards, and monitoring.

item.title: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro journalism to ChatGPT
item.description: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro’s journalism to ChatGPT through summaries and excerpts, with links to original stories.

item.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
item.description: See how Codex runs commands on your machine while enforcing the filesystem and network limits you control across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

item.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
item.description: OpenAI models optimized circuits used in Jalapeño silicon and improved RISC‑V core designs, showing progress in AI-assisted chip design with GPT‑6 Astra.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon

item.title: Genie 4 is now available
item.description: Genie 4 is now available

item.title: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices.
item.description: The Google Gemini app now supports lower-memory Android devices. Access Gemini Live and custom image creation on your phone. Download the app today.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for agentic coding, multistep tool use, and knowledge work.

item.title: Customize GitHub Copilot for your team
item.description: You can now share the GitHub Copilot plugins your team relies on without asking every member to repeat the same setup. Team customizations are generally available for organization teams.

item.title: Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot
item.description: You can now connect eight more services to Copilot using GitHub-verified MCP servers, or connectors, available in public preview. They join more than 25 services you can already connect, like Slack, Figma, and Sentry.

item.title: Anthropic prices initial public offering
item.description: Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock.

item.title: Announcements
item.description: Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.

item.title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
item.description: How OpenAI is working with NATO and allied cyber agencies to help trusted defenders find vulnerabilities, test fixes and protect essential systems.

item.title: Introducing OpenAI for Chile
item.description: OpenAI and the Government of Chile are partnering to support responsible AI adoption, build public-sector skills and help local startups develop AI applications.

item.title: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
item.description: Introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, with better professional outputs, coding, computer use, and efficiency at lower cost across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales
item.description: Explore the new Sales plugin and 30+ new and expanded partner plugins in ChatGPT to research prospects, prepare pitches, update your CRM, and move deals forward.

item.title: background completion window
item.description: Choose a two-hour or eight-hour background completion window in the Responses API public beta. Model token rates are 30% lower than Standard for the two-hour window and 40% lower for the eight-hour window.

item.title: Astra for Law leads in legal intelligence
item.description: Astra for Law ranked first in a launch evaluation spanning 24 areas of law. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.

item.title: Put Gemini to work for you
item.description: Tasks in Gemini is now free of charge in six countries, with new features starting in the U.S. and deeper Google Workspace integration to get things done on your behalf.

item.title: AlphaGenome available without an allowlist
item.description: Change AlphaGenome available without an allowlist AlphaGenome ( alphagenome-003 and alphagenome-004 ) no longer requires project allowlisting. Any Google Cloud project can view and deploy AlphaGenome from Model Garden without submitting an access request. For deployment requirements, see AlphaGenome.

item.title: Upcoming deprecation of MAI-Code-1.1-Flash in December
item.description: With the launch of MAI Code 2 Flash, we will deprecate MAI-Code-1.1-Flash across all GitHub Copilot experiences on December 18, 2026: Model Deprecation date Suggested alternative MAI-Code-1.1-Flash 2026-12-18 Latest MAI Code Flash model Please update your workflows and integrations to use the new model before December 18. Copilot Enterprise administrators may need to enable access to the alternative model through their model policies in Copilot settings.

item.title: Track Copilot code review outcomes in Repository insights
item.description: You can now see how Copilot code review feedback lands in each repository. A new “Repository insights” page, the first item in a repository’s Insights tab, brings Copilot code review outcomes together in one place.

item.title: Secret scanning on demand for developers and agents
item.description: Secret scanning should keep pace with the way you build software, whether you write code yourself or work with an AI agent. Copilot’s security review specialist now runs GitHub secret scanning, so developers and agents can catch secrets in code changes before they’re merged.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol now available
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now generally available in GitHub Copilot. Both models are designed for agentic coding and code review, with stronger coding judgment than earlier GPT-6 models.

item.title: Monitor GitHub Copilot activity through Microsoft Agent 365
item.description: Enterprises can now stream GitHub Copilot agent activity directly into Microsoft Agent 365. This lets you bring audit data from across GitHub Copilot clients into Microsoft’s agent control plane, where you can review Copilot activity alongside other AI workloads.

item.title: MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot
item.description: The next generation of Microsoft AI (MAI) coding models has arrived in GitHub Copilot. Introducing MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, two new models that represent a major step forward for the MAI-Code family, expanding from lightweight coding assistance to complex, agentic software engineering.

item.title: Let GitHub Copilot interact with your browser
item.description: Paired with the GitHub Copilot Chrome extension, browser use is now available in public preview in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, VS Code and JetBrains. This is part of our ongoing effort to bring computer use into developers’ everyday workflows, making it easier to work with Copilot in the tools they already use.

item.title: GitHub Event Streams is now in preview
item.description: GitHub is now a real-time coordination layer between developers, agents, and automation. With Event Streams, your agent sleeps while there’s no work and wakes as soon as there is.

item.title: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains, Ignite releases
item.description: This update brings remote access, on-device voice dictation, and browser use controls to GitHub Copilot for JetBrains. Copilot users in JetBrains IDEs also get context usage shortcuts, historical diffs, simpler follow-up controls, and improvements to chat reliability.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion updates: more availability, benchmarks, and models
item.description: Today, we’re expanding GitHub Copilot Fusion with new models, available on more Copilot surfaces, and results on two public Terminal-Bench leaderboards, giving you more ways to use Fusion and compare its performance. GitHub Copilot Fusion joins public Terminal-Bench 4.1 leaderboard Copilot Fusion is now listed on Terminal-Bench 4.1 public leaderboards hosted by Stanford, Harbor, and the Laude Institute: Terminal-Bench 4.1 measures how well AI agents complete hard, realistic tasks in a terminal.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Evals is now in public preview
item.description: You can now use GitHub Copilot Evals to optimize GitHub Copilot for yourself. As your prompts, models, skills, and tools change, are you still getting the most out of Copilot?

item.title: GitHub Copilot CLI adds Microsoft Entra sign-in as a preview
item.description: GitHub Copilot CLI now supports Microsoft Entra authentication in public preview. You can sign in with your Microsoft Entra account to silently authenticate to a linked GitHub Enterprise Managed User (EMU) account, use your Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or both, depending on your organization’s entitlements.

item.title: GitHub Copilot app, Microsoft Ignite releases
item.description: Copilot is most useful when it can work where you do. The GitHub Copilot app now supports your Azure DevOps repositories, your GitHub Enterprise Server instance, and the browser you’re already signed in to.

item.title: Copilot code review: Adaptive effort, secret detection, and more
item.description: GitHub Copilot code review now helps you catch more issues earlier, with less effort. Adaptive matches review depth to each pull request, so routine changes get a quick pass and risky changes get a deeper look.

item.title: user-profiles-billing-2026-10-01
item.description: We’ve launched Linked billing in beta with the user-profiles-billing-2026-10-01 beta header. Your customers can now pay for the Claude usage in your app through their own Claude organization. Once a customer links their organization, set billing_policy on each /v1/messages or /v1/chat/completions request to choose who pays. In the Claude Console, customers can set a spend cap for your app or unlink your app.

item.title: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership
item.description: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch a £1m partnership to help up to 25,000 young people across the UK build practical AI skills for work.

item.title: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support
item.description: New tools, practical guidance, and partnerships will help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

item.title: Science at the Frontier: How scientists use ChatGPT
item.description: Explore how more than 1,800 scientists use ChatGPT in research. See findings on daily workflows, reported productivity, and expectations for discovery.

item.title: How Revolut raises ambition without lowering the bar
item.description: Discover how Revolut uses OpenAI models and Codex to cut coding time by 30–60%, scale financial crime investigations, and innovate without compromising security.

item.title: Our first phase of embedded assessments
item.description: OpenAI begins embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, and Transluce, and Goodfire to independently evaluate model alignment, safeguards, and monitoring systems.

item.title: More ways to move care forward with ChatGPT for Healthcare
item.description: Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.

item.title: LVMH’s Media Division announces strategic partnership with OpenAI
item.description: LVMH’s Media Division and OpenAI announce a partnership to support journalism with AI and make its publications more accessible through ChatGPT.

item.title: At Holiday Extras, dots get to work before anyone asks
item.description: Dots deliver launch reports unprompted, flag issues people might miss, and talk through upcoming meetings on the commute to work.
